newsitem.title: ESTONIA: BANK ASSETS REACH 24.8 BLN KROONS IN MARCH.
newsitem.headline: BANK ASSETS REACH 24.8 BLN KROONS IN MARCH.

text.p: The combined balance sheet of commercial banks was 24.8 billion kroons in March compared to 23 billion kroons in February, the central bank said on Tuesday.
The change represents an increase in the banks' balance sheet of 8.2 percent compared to the previous month, the central bank said in a statement.
Deposits in banks increased by 1.7 percent to 15.3 billion kroons from February's 15 billion kroons.
Hansapank and Hoiupank had the largest share of deposits, both with 24 percent. Uhispank had 16 percent of deposits.
Uhispank had most government funds held in banks with 37.3 percent of the total of 2.6 billion kroons.
Next came Hoiupank with 19.4 percent and Pohja-Eesti Pank, which has been merged with Uhispank, had 10 percent.
The combined amount of government money held by Uhispank and PEP is equal to 47.3 percent of the government funds held by banks in Estonia, the central bank said.
Loan to individuals rose to 2.2 billion kroons from 2.0 billion kroons. Hoiupank has lent just under one billion kroons and holds 45.2 percent of the total amount lent by commercial banks.
